question: R-046 parity gate failed before any development case ran. The gate (R-042 criterion: zero sustained flips, <= 4/40 diverged) compared the frozen gait via R-039's run_cell with the backend's unchanged scaffold on 40 cases (seed 4184). Result: 37/40 environments bit-identical in spin_rate and center_dist for all 359 steps; 3 environments diverge only late, first differing at steps 340, 185 and 260 (GPU PhysX at batch 40 is not bit-deterministic across processes, as D-035 documented: 1-2/40 envs diverge after step ~78). One of them (env 20, divergence from step 260) flips: reference sustained with tail-hit 1.0, backend not sustained with tail-hit 0.783; successes 22 vs 21. The gate's purpose here (call_00094) was to check that the wrapped scaffold reproduces the gait; identical trajectories in 37 envs and late-only divergence say the wrapper is exact and the flip is physics nondeterminism on a marginal episode. The study stopped as coded; no further episode or LLM call was spent (80 parity episodes). Options: (a) amend the gate before any development case, R-039-style, to a wrapper-equivalence criterion: every environment bit-identical through step 150 (no divergence before half the episode) and at most 4/40 diverged environments overall, flips reported but not gating; then continue with the same frozen manifests (parity cases are not reused by any arm); (b) rerun parity on a fresh seed (spends 80 more episodes, risks selecting on a passing draw); (c) stop R-046 inconclusive. I recommend (a). Which do you approve?
